title: Dual finite-free system criterion for flat Mittag-Leffler modules
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $M$ be a flat $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed partially ordered set, and let $(M_i,f_{ij})_{i\in I}$ be a system of finite free $R$-modules whose compatible maps $f_i:M_i\to M$ exhibit $M$ as its colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Suppose that the inverse system of dual modules is Mittag-Leffler, meaning explicitly that for every $i\in I$ there exists $j\ge i$ such that for every $k\ge j$ the images of the precomposition maps $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_k,R)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_i,R)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_j,R)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_i,R)$ are equal. Then $M$ is Mittag-Leffler in the tensor-product sense [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module].

source.place: Tag 059G (remark-flat-ML); directed-index Mittag-Leffler condition spelled out as in Tag 0595 (definition-ML-system)

proof.text: Fix $i\in I$, and choose $j\ge i$ by the dual Mittag-Leffler hypothesis. Choose a finite basis $(e_a)_{a=1}^n$ of $M_j$ with coordinate maps $\epsilon_a:M_j\to R$. For each $k\ge j$, the map $\epsilon_a\circ f_{ij}$ belongs to the image of $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_j,R)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_i,R)$, hence by the chosen image equality there is $\lambda_{a,k}:M_k\to R$ with $\lambda_{a,k}\circ f_{ik}=\epsilon_a\circ f_{ij}$. Define the linear map $h_k:M_k\to M_j$ by $h_k(y)=\sum_{a=1}^n\lambda_{a,k}(y)e_a$. For every $x\in M_i$ the basis expansion gives $h_k(f_{ik}(x))=\sum_a\epsilon_a(f_{ij}(x))e_a=f_{ij}(x)$, so $h_k\circ f_{ik}=f_{ij}$. For $n=0$ this is the zero map into $M_j=0$. Thus a single $j$, chosen before any tensor test module, gives these factorizations for every $k\ge j$.

source.place: Tag 059G (remark-flat-ML), finite-free dual argument expanded in coordinates; Tag 059E (proposition-ML-characterization), factorization condition (3).

proof.text: Let $L$ be any $R$-module and $z\in\ker(f_i\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-commutes-with-colimits], the maps $f_s\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L$ exhibit $M\otimes_R L$ as the colimit of the directed system $M_s\otimes_R L$. Apply the zero criterion of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] to $z$ at stage $i$: there is $k_0\ge i$ with $(f_{ik_0}\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L)(z)=0$. Choose a common upper bound $k\ge k_0,j$. Then $f_{ik}=f_{k_0k}\circ f_{ik_0}$, so tensor functoriality [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives $(f_{ik}\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L)(z)=0$. Smallness, nonemptiness and directedness are exactly those in the given system; tensoring does not change its index set.

source.place: Tag 059E (proposition-ML-characterization), proof of (3) implies (2); Tag 00DD (lemma-tensor-products-commute-with-limits); Tag 00D7 (lemma-zero-directed-limit).

proof.text: For this $k\ge j$, Step 1 and the composition identity in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] give $(f_{ij}\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L)(z)=(h_k\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L)((f_{ik}\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L)(z))=0$. Therefore $\ker(f_i\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L)\subseteq\ker(f_{ij}\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L)$ for every $L$. The index $j$ depends only on $i$; the auxiliary $k$ may depend on $L,z$. This is precisely domination of $f_i$ by $f_{ij}$.

source.place: Tag 059E (proposition-ML-characterization), proof of (3) implies (2), tensor-kernel inclusion.

proof.text: Each $M_s$ is finitely presented [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]: a chosen isomorphism $R^{n_s}\to M_s$ gives the finite presentation $R^0\to R^{n_s}\to M_s\to0$. Apply [lem-trf-mittag-leffler-eventual-domination] to the given directed colimit of these finitely presented modules. Steps 1--3 give exactly its condition that for every $i$ some $j\ge i$ makes $f_{ij}$ dominate $f_i$. Its reverse implication concludes that $M$ is Mittag-Leffler in the tensor-product sense, as required. The assumed flatness is retained in the statement; the proof needs only the supplied finite-free colimit presentation.

source.place: Tags 059E (proposition-ML-characterization), condition (2), and 059M (proposition-ML-tensor), tensor-product characterization; Tag 059G (remark-flat-ML).
